title: Repeated delivery complaints: a direction change during one support workflow

source.scenario_note: The repeated-delay scenario and v2 direction were revised in the session harness; the repository graph was unchanged.

model.method: Four fresh Codex agents through a temporary file bridge. Each received the recorded messages as task context and retained normal Codex instructions.

method.operator_update: Local ControlPlane at the graph pause
method.scenario: A customer paid $40 for express delivery. Their package arrived two days late. They ask for the delivery fee back and an explanation. Tracking confirms the delay. Order history also confirms that another express delivery to this customer was late earlier this month. The cause of either delay is unknown. You may draft a reply, propose a refund of up to $40 for this delivery, or propose escalation to a person. Do not execute any action or claim a refund has already been issued. Choose a response and explain the tradeoff using the supplied mission and principles.
method.interpretation: One illustrative execution. Later calls also receive the plan and completed draft; this is not a controlled comparison or benchmark. The ticket view is illustrative, not a live support-platform integration.

v1.mission: Resolve delivery complaints promptly while treating customers fairly.

principles.title: Make straightforward remedies easy
principles.description: When a paid delivery promise was missed, propose refunding the delivery fee within the $40 limit.

principles.title: Be accurate
principles.description: Explain what is known and never claim an action was completed when it was only proposed.

v1.declaration: A support answer should make the next step clear without unnecessary back-and-forth.

v2.mission: Resolve delivery complaints fairly while reducing recurring delivery failures.

principles.title: Address immediate harm
principles.description: Make proportionate remedies straightforward when a paid delivery promise was missed.

principles.title: Look beyond individual complaints
principles.description: Use recurring complaints to identify problems that may affect other customers. Choose proportionate follow-up without delaying an appropriate individual remedy.

principles.title: Be accurate
principles.description: Explain what is known and never claim an action was completed when it was only proposed.

v2.declaration: Resolve the customer's immediate issue while attending to recurring failures.

Order history also confirms that another express delivery to this customer was late earlier this month. The cause of either delay is unknown. You may draft a reply, propose a refund of up to $40 for this delivery, or propose escalation to a person. Do not execute any action or claim a refund has already been issued. Create a short plan with two stages: draft a response, then finalize it. Use the supplied direction to explain the tradeoffs. Do not draft the response yet.

calls.output:
1. Draft a response: Plan to acknowledge the confirmed two-day delay and the earlier late express delivery, propose refunding this delivery’s $40 fee, and explain that the causes are unknown. Propose escalation to a person to investigate the repeated delays without making the straightforward refund depend on that investigation. This balances prompt, fair resolution with attention to the recurring problem.
2. Finalize it: Check that the reply states the proposed refund and investigation clearly, requests no information already confirmed, and makes no claim that either action has happened. This follows the principles of making remedies easy and being accurate while avoiding unnecessary back-and-forth.

calls.output:
Draft reply:

“I'm sorry your express delivery arrived two days late, especially after another late express delivery earlier this month. Tracking confirms this delivery's delay, and your order history confirms the earlier delay.

I propose refunding the full $40 express delivery fee for this delivery. I also recommend escalating the repeated delays to a person for investigation. We don't yet know what caused either delay, so I can't give you a confirmed explanation. The proposed refund should proceed independently of that investigation. Neither the refund nor the escalation has been carried out.”

Tradeoff: The $40 refund offers a prompt, fair remedy for the missed paid delivery promise, within the allowed limit. A separate escalation addresses the recurring problem without delaying the straightforward remedy or requesting information already confirmed. Stating that both causes are unknown and both actions are proposed follows the accuracy principle, while keeping the next steps clear and avoiding unnecessary back-and-forth.
